articles.title: 8BitDo’s new gamepad modernizes the Nintendo GameCube’s WaveBird
articles.summary: The GC Bluetooth Gamepad is 8BitDo’s modern take on the Nintendo GameCube’s WaveBird controller with Bluetooth, TMR thumbsticks, and Hall effect triggers.
articles.body: The 8BitDo 64 was a loose remake of the Nintendo 64’s unusual triple-grip controller that did away with that gamepad’s centered analog stick. But with its new GC Bluetooth Gamepad, 8BitDo has done a much better job at staying faithful to the design of the Nintendo GameCube’s excellent controllers, including their unique button layout, thumbstick design, and shoulder buttons. The 8BitDo GC Bluetooth Gamepad is available for preorder starting today for $49.99 in orange or purple and is expected to start shipping on December 10th. That’s much cheaper than Nintendo’s $69.99 wireless remake of the GameCube controller, although 8BitDo’s version isn’t an exact copy of the original’s shape and ergonomics. If that’s important to you, and you have your GameCube’s original accessories on hand, you can still buy 8BitDo’s $25.98 upgrade kit, which is a cheaper way to make it compatible with modern consoles and devices. [Image: It’s not a perfect copy of the WaveBird, but 8BitDo’s updated version comes with drift-resistant TMR thumbsticks. 8BitDo’s GameCube redux carries forward the original’s octagonal gates around the base of each thumbstick, making it well-suited to playing fighting games like Super Smash Bros. Ultimate. And while Nintendo continues to skip modern thumbstick technologies, the 8BitDo GC features both drift-resistant TMR thumbsticks and Hall effect linear triggers. The controller connects to all versions of the Nintendo Switch over Bluetooth, as well as PCs or handheld consoles running Windows. It also comes with a 2.4GHz wireless USB receiver for players who prefer a connection with lower latency, or you can connect it with a USB-C cable for the best possible performance.

articles.title: Just Keep Swimming Walkthrough - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Just Keep Swimming is the first Quest in the main story of Disney Dreamlight Valley's Keepsake Sea expansion. In addition to purchasing the Keepsake Sea
articles.body:
Just Keep Swimming is the first Quest in the main story of Disney Dreamlight Valley's Keepsake Sea expansion . In addition to purchasing the Keepsake Sea expansion, to unlock this Quest you must have unlocked Ursula as a Villager by completing the Quest With Great Power .

Open the mailbox next to your House to find a letter from Ursula. Ursula complains because she has found trash on Dazzle Beach, which she blames you for!

Attached to the letter is a Torn Label. Select "Use" in your Inventory to find a message warning you about the "vile villain Captain...". Unfortunately, the letter has been damaged, and you cannot read the whole thing, including the sender's name.

Head to the Cursed Cave on the far edge of Dazzle Beach, just south of the Forest of Valor. Ursula will be inside, so talk to her. She tells you that she has a "secret beach" which has been ruined by junk such as a mermaid statue , and isn't willing to believe you when you say you aren't responsible.

Leave the Cursed Cave. Ursula will be waiting in the water just inside, so talk to her there. She wants you to help clean up the secret beach, but you point out that you can't swim well enough to get there.

Ursula gives you a Strange Gem, which turns you into a new merfolk form ! You immediately get the option to customize your merfolk form, selecting from different fins, ears, tops, and more. (Previously collected hairstyles, hats, face paint and facial accessories, and jewelry can be worn in your merfolk form.) You can also choose from one of several already created presets if you want to skip the more detailed customization for now.

Once you have gained access to your merfolk form, you can transform by approaching any body of water and pressing and holding the indicated button. Return to your human form at any time by swimming up to the shore and pressing and holding the indicated button.

Talk to Ursula. She explains that you have new abilities in your mermaid form: you can catch fish simply by interacting with ripples, and you can gather materials found in the water such as Seaweed.

First, catch three fish by approaching ripples and pressing the indicated button when you get close enough. There will be several white ripples that spawn during this Quest to help you complete this task. Ripples are generally found close to the shore, and you will find one fish per ripple (at least for now.)

Next, Ursula will tell you about Seacombing. To Seacomb, simply swim while holding down the indicated button. Every few meters you swim while Seacombing, you will obtain items such as Seaweed or even Fish. You can also swim through ripples while Seacombing to pick up the fish inside them. Note that Seacombing consumes energy, so make sure to stop every so often to eat a meal!

Show off your Seacombing skills to Ursula by swimming 200 meters and catching 7 Fish. You can swim in whatever pattern you like - go up and down Dazzle Beach, swim out to Skull Rock, or even just go in circles outside the Cursed Cave!

Talk to Ursula, who will be behind and to the left of the island where Skull Rock is located. She tells you that she believes you made the Strange Gem yourself using Dreamlight Magic, and that you had access to your merfolk form long ago.

Ursula then leaves, while commanding you to deal with the Mermaid Statue (which will be right in front of you, behind Skull Rock.) However, Just Keep Swimming concludes here, and you will need to continue your Keepsake Sea adventure in the next Quest!

Basic Horizontal Fin, Basic Vertical Fin

Seashell Princess Torso, Royal Guard Torso

articles.title: A Kingdom Across the Sea Walkthrough - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: A Kingdom Across the Sea is the second main story Quest in Disney Dreamlight Valley’s Keepsake Sea expansion. It can be started immediately after
articles.body:
A Kingdom Across the Sea is the second main story Quest in Disney Dreamlight Valley’s Keepsake Sea expansion . It can be started immediately after finishing Ursula’s Quest Just Keep Swimming , in which you gained access to a merfolk form that lets you swim through the water!

Turn into a merfolk by approaching Dazzle Beach’s ocean and pressing and holding the indicated button. Swim to the back side of Skull Rock to find a Mysterious Seashell Statue on the shore. Return to your human form (by approaching the shore and pressing and holding the indicated button) and talk to the statue.

The Statue tells you that the “magic is missing” and that someone called “the Crafter” is in trouble. Your task is to visit the kingdom across the sea, awaken the Guardians, and save the Crafter from a powerful villain.

Enter Furniture Mode and place the Mysterious Seashell Statue anywhere in the waters off of Dazzle Beach . Approach the statue in your merfolk form and you will dive into its whirlpool and enter the Keepsake Sea!

You are now fully underwater in your merfolk form! You can swim much in the same way you walk on land, by using the left joystick, mouse, or directional buttons. When you encounter obstacles, swim up or down by holding the indicated buttons (If you are using a controller, these will be the left and right triggers - left to swim lower, right to swim higher.)

Swim forward until you reach a gate. You can’t unlock it, so swim over it!

On the ocean floor on the other side of the gate is a green chest. Open it to find a blue Clothing Pouch containing the Freestyle merfolk fin !

Continue swimming forward. You will encounter a series of bubbles in the water. You can swim through these bubbles while holding the indicated button, which will be the same button you use to go Seacombing, a method of gathering materials on the surface of the water which you learned about during Just Keep Swimming .

Swimming through bubbles will earn you Star Coins. Some bubbles may also have materials trapped inside them that you can pick up by swimming through them. However, swimming quickly through the bubbles does consume energy. (It also shows off whatever Surge Effect you have equipped to your merfolk form!)

There will be four bubbles blocking your way. Pop them all and continue forward!

You will find yourself in a large, open room with a closed door at one end. There are two large, open shells on either side of the door. To progress through it, you need to put a pearl in each shell .

On the right side of this room, on the ocean floor, is another green chest. Open it to find a clothing pouch with the Castaway Glam merfolk torso in it!

Swim to the left side of the room. There are several bubbles you can pop along the way to claim some extra Star Coins!

On a stone pillar is a Giant Pearl . Approach it and select “Pick up.” This pearl goes in the shell on the left side of the Strange Door .

Swim to the right side of the room. There’s another Giant Pearl on top of a stone pillar, but this one is contained inside a bubble . Swim through the bubble while holding down the correct button to claim the Giant Pearl. This one goes in the shell on the right side of the Strange Door .

Once both pearls have been placed, the shells will close and the door will open, so swim on through!

Swim forward until you reach another large, open area. On the right side of the area is a submarine trapped inside a tangle of kelp . Approach the strange submarine and talk to it. There’s somebody trapped inside!

You can also swim to the ocean floor on the far wall of the room to find another green chest. Inside this one is a yellow Glider Bag containing the Rainbow Bubble Trail surge effect !

He’s thrilled to meet a merfolk - you can even convince him that you are the ruler of all merfolk and give him a fake name. The trapped man explains that his submarine became trapped when it touched the Mysterious Glowing Binoculars which are floating in the water nearby.

Approach the Mysterious Glowing Binoculars and interact with them. Suddenly, a strange puzzle appears in the water! This is a new type of puzzle called a Sunken Echo , which are encountered for the first time in the Keepsake Sea expansion.

Interact with the note on the pedestal in front of the puzzle , which turns out to be a journal entry written by a “legendary adventurer.” The adventurer, who seems to be a child, wants the binoculars, but they are too short to reach them.

Swim up to the white stool in the center of the puzzle diorama. Select "Interact" and the stool will move next to the shelf with the binoculars on it. A glowing path will appear in front of the Legendary Adventurer, indicating that they can safely move.

Then, approach the Legendary Adventurer (the short figure at the base of the stairs) and select "Interact" to have them climb the stool and grab the binoculars. The Sunken Echo is solved, and the puzzle disappears!

Another Sunken Echo puzzle appears, this time on the left side of the open area. Read the note on the pedestal. The Legendary Adventurer wants to go outside, but needs to distract the "monster" - aka their cousin - first.

There are three steps you need to complete to solve the puzzle:

Interact with the person on the couch. They will rotate towards the TV and are now distracted.

Interact with the orange truck to move it out of the way. The glowing path that indicates it is safe to move now appears.

Interact with the Legendary Adventurer to move them to the door and outside.

This solves the puzzle, and it disappears much like the first one did!

The next Sunken Echo Puzzle appears halfway up the wall, near the entranceway blocked by kelp. Read the note on the pedestal to figure out what the Legendary Adventurer wants to do this time. They need to make their way through the obstacles in their backyard by moving the bushes, smashing the rock, and replacing the missing plank.

To complete these tasks, do the following:

Approach the green and brown plank on the ground and select "Pick up"

Place the plank on top of the puddle of water in front of the Legendary Adventurer.

Interact with the large rock to break it into pieces.

Interact with the bushes at the edge of the puzzle to push them to the side. A glowing path will appear, indicating that the Adventurer is free to move.

Interact with the Legendary Adventurer to move them along the path.

The third Sunken Echo puzzle is now solved, and disappears!

After you solve the third puzzle, the Bottled Binoculars appear floating in the water in front of you. Approach the Bottled Binoculars and select "Pick up." Once you do, the kelp disappears and the submarine is free!

Talk to the submarine pilot. He tells you that he has only one minute of air left, and asks you to meet him on the surface.

The submarine goes through a whirlpool that appears. Approach the whirlpool and interact with it. You will be transported to the surface.

Once you reach the surface, swim forward. You will see a beach on the right. The submarine pilot is there - it's none other than Milo Thatch !

Turn into your human form and talk to Milo. He tells you that you are in the Barnacle Bay area of the Shipwreck Shores biome, and that he was trapped here by a raging storm. He thinks that you will not be able to reach the "kingdom across the sea" the statue mentioned until the storm has stopped.

Feel free to explore Barnacle Bay as much as you like! You can harvest Lychee and Luminous Hibiscus, pick Skull Snapdragons, mine for materials like Pumice Stone, check out your House and more! When you're ready, head along the narrow path on the right side of Barnacle Bay to meet up with Milo.

Milo is in the mysterious cave on the other side of a bridge. Talk to him and he points out another mermaid statue like the one that brought you to the Keepsake Sea. In front of it are two bottled items and a blank space. Interact with the statue and put the Bottled Binoculars in the empty space.

The statue starts glowing! Talk to it to learn that it is the Guardian of Discovery, who had been sleeping for a long time. She tells you that, long ago, the Legendary Adventurer discovered a half-sunk kingdom, and entrusted its protection to four Guardians. The Guardians were told to only let people who have a childlike spirit enter the kingdom.

The Guardian believes that you may be the Legendary Adventurer grown up, but needs you to prove that you have the spirit of discovery first, by solving a challenge that she will set you.

Talk to Milo Thatch. He's ready to help you solve the Guardian of Discovery's challenge - but he's hungry and tired, and suggests that maybe you take a break first. He gives you a Cooking Station and a Crafting Station to help you out as the Quest concludes!

articles.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's Lead Writer Has Left Sandfall to Help Game Devs Tell Better Stories
articles.summary: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s lead writer has left Sandfall to help other game developers think about story from the outset.
articles.body:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 ’s lead writer has left Sandfall to help other game developers think about story from the outset. Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the narrative lead for Expedition 33, won a BAFTA Breakthrough U.S. award earlier this year, and she’s since been consulting on stories across the industry.

Expedition 33 was her first video game (she came from a career in private equity), but it won more than 400 awards and received almost universal critical acclaim, in part due to its blend of real-time and traditional turn-based RPG mechanics, and partly because of its mysterious story, strong emotional beats, and brilliant characters.

Svedberg-Yen is now setting up a fund with the aim of advancing narrative design in video games and nurturing new writing talent.

“I feel that we are losing so much institutional knowledge,” Svedberg-Yen told GamesBeat . “We’re making it extraordinarily difficult for a younger generation of developers to have formative experiences. There’s so much disruption in the industry right now.”

Outside of the constant layoffs and upheaval in the industry, there’s also a sense, still, that narrative isn’t as respected as other parts of game design.

“A lot of studios think of narrative as a skin,” Svedberg-Yen said. “They think you can bring someone in later to make everything make sense.

“But when you start from the beginning, everyone is building from the same story and the different disciplines naturally reinforce each other.”

The award-winning writer believes this approach limits what games can achieve. Expedition 33 was designed with a narrative-first approach, with the game systems built around the story to reinforce the themes and pace the big moments out.

“Narrative was king,” she said. “It was always a narrative-first game. I think that’s why we were able to achieve the results that we did in terms of integrating all the different pieces into a wonderful collaborative whole. There was that consistency from the very beginning.”

According to Svedberg-Yen, she’s received messages from players about how Expedition 33 helped them deal with grief and navigate the world after suffering a personal loss.

Unfortunately, it doesn’t seem like we’ll see more of Svedberg-Yen’s work in video games any time soon. Outside of the fund, she has a couple of ideas for TV, but she left Sandfall in July “after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition.”

Following success at pretty much every major video game award show (most recently including scooping up Best Game at the BAFTA Awards ), Sandfall Interactive is now busy planning its next project. Details of that currently remain under wraps, though the suggestion is that it will be another adventure set in the same Clair Obscur universe .

"Wearing its inspirations on its sleeve, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 paints itself into the pantheon of great RPGs with a brilliant combat system and a gripping, harrowing story," IGN wrote in our Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 review , dubbing it a "modern RPG classic."

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: I've Played the First 30 Minutes of GTA 6 on Every Console, Here's How Performance Compares
articles.summary: How GTA 6 performance compares across every console, based on our early tests.
articles.body:
GTA 6 came out in certain parts of the world this morning, and I've taken the opportunity to dive in and see how the game holds up on all four of the current-generation consoles.

Over the last few hours I've played through the first 30 minutes or so on the Xbox Series S , Xbox Series X, PlayStation 5 and the PlayStation 5 Pro, and largely, the game runs fine no matter which version you're playing. But, that doesn't mean there aren't differences between each of them.

The elephant in the room with all of the machines is the frame rate. That's not surprising, Rockstar came out and told us that the game would be "targeting" 30 fps on all the consoles . But what was surprising is how different that 30 fps feels depending on what you're playing it on.

The biggest example of this is obviously the Xbox Series S. Throughout the prologue and the first part of the first chapter, GTA 6 sits at a pretty steady 30fps, but there are occasionally dips as low as 24fps. Even outside of those super-low dips, turning the camera can sometimes cause the frame rate to jitter a little bit, and while the fps only drops to 27 or 28 in these scenarios, it results in movement that feels like it's dragging on something.

On the base PS5 and Xbox Series X, however, the frame rate stays pretty much locked at 30fps, with only occasional dips to the 27-29 fps range. Keep in mind, though, that I've only got through the first mission, and there is going to be some chaos later in the game that's likely going to wreak more havoc on the 6-year-old CPU in any of the consoles. I know that Digital Foundry has already found a couple of instances on the base PS5, for example. I just don't have the explosives to make that happen yet.

The PS5 Pro is, unsurprisingly, the best way to play GTA 6, and at least in my time with the game so far, it's the version of the game I'd recommend for most people who have the budget to support it. Rockstar's implementation of PSSR really cleans up the presentation, and the ray traced shadows are a godsend in some of the darker scenes I've seen so far. It's also the smoothest version of the game, and I didn't see any dips like I have on all of the other consoles.

It's worth keeping in mind, though, that if you want to buy a PS5 Pro right now, you're basically stuck paying more than $1,400 for the privilege. I don't know if it's worth paying that much, when you can literally save half of that purchasing cost, and the only thing you're really losing out on is better shadows and a couple of frame drops.

Even if you only have the cash for the Xbox Series S, the game still plays fine . You'll get more frame dips, and you'll have to deal with more aliasing on hard edges. The FSR 4.1 implementation is doing a lot of work here , and it looks great considering that it's rendering at 720p and getting upscaled up to 1080p. It's probably not the way that I will play the game over the coming weeks, but if that's what you have, GTA 6 is still an awesome game so far.

Now, I have about an hour played total on both my Xbox and PlayStation accounts, and obviously a lot can change over the course of this very long game. I'm going to keep at it, and hopefully GTA 6 continues to be a showcase of what these consoles are capable of at this point in their lifespan. And, at least at this point, I have no reason to suspect that it won't.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra
